title: A finite simplicial lifting problem for a hypercover is locally solvable
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $K_\bullet\to X$ an etale hypercover: its terms are objects of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and each term covers its matching object. For a simplicial set $S$ with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, $\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ denotes the semi-representable object over $X$ characterized by its etale test-scheme points: a point over $T\to X$ is a compatible family of maps $T\to K_m$, one for each $m$-simplex of $S$, respecting every face and degeneracy operator (and choosing a component whenever a term of $K$ is a family). Let $A\subseteq B$ be an inclusion of simplicial sets, both with finitely many nondegenerate simplices and with finite nonempty sets of simplices in each degree. The restriction $\operatorname{Hom}(B,K)_0\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,K)_0$ is an etale covering in the category of semi-representable objects over $X$. Thus compatible $A$-data represented on an etale test scheme extend to $B$ after an etale covering of that test scheme.
